newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUBGY UNION - FORGET CALIFANO, HERE COMES CASADEI.
newsitem.headline: RUBGY UNION - FORGET CALIFANO, HERE COMES CASADEI.

text.p: Scotland might have been relieved to hear that French prop Christian Califano would miss Saturday's crucial Five Nations' clash but his replacement, Didier Casadei, promises to be just as hot to handle.
The 25-year-old Casadei, who earned his first cap after Califano was suspended for punching an opponent in a league match at the weekend, is every bit like Califano.
Not only are both men dynamic, tough props but they look exactly the same with their massive bodies, shaven heads, broken noses and bruised eyebrows.

"It's true that they are very much alike physically but what interested us is that Casadei is the same kind of player as Califano," said French team manager Jo Maso. "He should fit in without any problem."

Califano's uppercut on Grenoble prop Louis Esposito's chin on Sunday came as embarrassing news to the French selectors, who have stated that any player sent off in a league match would automatically be suspended for the next international.
"It's a nuisance but it's a rule and rules must apply to everybody," said French coach Jean-Claude Skrela.

"I would have preferred to be picked in other circumstances but it's okay, I'll manage," said Casadei. "To play a first international with so much at stake is a great opportunity and I don't want to miss it."
If France beat Scotland, they would complete the fourth grand slam in their history, their first in 10 years and the first ever in Paris.
"I know how important the match is, you don't have to tell me," said Casadei.
As with Califano, things have not always been easy for Casadei, who helped Brive lift this year's European Cup.
